summary.headline: Caliber Q1 FY27 revenue rose to INR657 crore (vs INR393 crore), but reported EBITDA margin fell to 16.8%, or 20.02% adjusted, on diesel costs.
summary.overview: Revenue for Q1 FY27 was INR657 crore against INR393 crore a year earlier, with coal mining services contributing about 91% (INR597 crore). Reported EBITDA was INR110 crore, a 16.8% margin, which management says was 20.02% after adding back INR10.57 crore of diesel escalation recovered from Coal India. Cash profit rose to INR68.54 crore from INR55.37 crore, though PAT margin was lower because of higher depreciation and interest from Q1 capex. Management attributed the margin dip to the Iran-war diesel spike and guided FY27 revenue growth of 45-50%, EBITDA growth of 35%+ and PAT growth of 35%+.

segments.name: Coal mining services
segments.commentary: Contributed INR597 crore, about 91% of Q1 revenue; management cited 86% of FY26 revenue from mining. Q1 coal extraction 1.54 million tonnes (vs 1.21 million) and overburden removal 43.37 million cubic metres (vs 28.56 million).

segments.name: Coal logistics
segments.commentary: Road transport fell to 2.42 million tonnes from 2.98 million tonnes; rail loading rose to 4.77 million tonnes from 4.46 million tonnes. Logistics margin not disclosed separately; management says blended margins are similar.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of about 45-50% YoY, driven by full-year execution of recently won orders.
FY27 EBITDA growth of 35%+ YoY, subject to diesel cost normalisation; fleet and ERP efficiencies cited as drivers.
FY27 PAT growth of 35%+ YoY, helped by interest savings after IPO debt repayment.
Management sees normalised EBITDA margin of about 23% (range 22-25%) once fuel costs settle.
Q2 FY27 volumes guided at about 34 million cubic metres of overburden vs 43 million in Q1; Q3 and Q4 expected to be strongest after monsoon ends around 1 October.
Year-end FY27 debt expected around INR750 crore if no new tenders are added; about INR450 crore of new order value in FY27, of which INR167 crore is cash-funded and INR283 crore loan-funded.
risks_watch: Diesel price volatility and pass-through timing gaps; management's 23% normalised margin depends on fuel easing.
Customer concentration: over 80% of revenue from Coal India.
Penalty exposure if mine output falls short of contract volumes; management says shortfalls have been hindrances rather than inefficiency.
Monsoon-quarter volume drop (Q2 OB guided at 34 million cubic metres) and ramp-up at new sites.
Rising depreciation and interest from Q1 capex weighing on PAT; year-end debt and new-tender funding.
summary.management_tone: Confident on revenue and order book, but defensive on margin; management repeatedly described the diesel spike as one-off and blamed it for the dip. Answers on MDO, capex, guidance for FY28 and win rates were vague or deferred.

So we believe the worst in terms of spiking of diesel and scarcity of diesel is over, sir.
This is a one-off event, sir. This is not a cyclical event.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q1 margin compression one-off or will it continue through the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the dip to the Iran-war diesel spike, pointing to 20.02% adjusted EBITDA and a normalised ~23% margin once fuel eases; it called the diesel event one-off and cyclical in nature, with Q2 trend described as stabilising.

qa_highlights.question: Does the coal mining business have full fuel escalation clauses, and why did power and fuel cost rise from ~30% of revenue in FY22 to ~47% in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: All coal mining projects have fuel escalation, but timing mismatch means a small portion is absorbed. Management said the rise reflects the shift from logistics to mining, where fuel intensity is higher, and that mining was 86% of FY26 revenue versus 40-60% earlier.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company planning MDO and iron ore, and how will the capex be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, MDO coal, MDO iron ore and iron ore mining are being explored, along with one critical mineral block in Maharashtra. Funding is from IPO proceeds of INR167 crore for equipment and cash flow from lower EMIs; no capex figure was given for MDO.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company give FY27 and FY28 revenue and margin guidance, and what is the 2-3 year capex?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 guidance was given in closing remarks: revenue growth 45-50%, EBITDA growth 35%+, PAT growth 35%+. No FY28 guidance was given; capex for the next 2-3 years was deferred to a later date.

qa_highlights.question: What is the gross debt, cost of debt and year-end debt expectation?
qa_highlights.answer: Opening FY27 debt was INR1,024 crore, expected to fall to about INR750 crore at year-end without new tenders; average cost of debt 8.5-9%, expected to decline after the rating upgrade to A minus.

qa_highlights.question: What is the bidding pipeline and win rate, and are bids outside coal being pursued?
qa_highlights.answer: 8-10 tenders in coal and overburden are pending results; the company is evaluating iron ore and MDO projects on margin and ROCE. No win rate was disclosed; a tender list would be shared on email request.

qa_highlights.question: Why did PAT margin fall while EBITDA grew, and is the depreciation policy different?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Nikhil Karwa said higher depreciation and interest in Q1 from the quarter's higher capex, with the new assets not yet contributing a full quarter of revenue, explained the lower PAT margin; no change in depreciation policy was indicated.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Adani Power Parsa suspension and is any amount outstanding?
qa_highlights.answer: Work stopped after land issues at the site; equipment was moved to the Jayant site in Singrauli, Madhya Pradesh, to avoid idle cost. Management says there was no loss, and work has not restarted at Parsa though it remains in touch with Adani.

capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 operations: coal extraction 1.54 million tonnes (vs 1.21 million), overburden removal 43.37 million cubic metres (vs 28.56 million), road transport 2.42 million tonnes (vs 2.98 million), rail loading 4.77 million tonnes (vs 4.46 million); fleet size 2,033 as of June 2026.

IPO proceeds of INR500 crore: INR208 crore for debt repayment, INR167 crore for new equipment, INR125 crore for day-to-day expenses and liquidity (management corrected the INR175 crore figure to INR125 crore).
FY27 new order value of about INR450 crore, of which INR167 crore is cash-funded and INR283 crore loan-funded; management says INR50 crore variance possible either way.
Year-end FY27 gross debt expected around INR750 crore assuming no new tenders; opening FY27 debt was INR1,024 crore; average cost of debt 8.5-9%, expected to fall after the rating upgrade.

Q2 FY27 overburden volume guided at about 34 million cubic metres vs 43 million in Q1; Q3 and Q4 expected to be strongest after monsoon ends around 1 October. Management is evaluating MDO and iron ore opportunities against margin and ROCE, with no timeline given; a critical mineral block in Maharashtra is secured. Capex for the next 2-3 years to be guided later.
demand_pricing: Order book INR9,124 crore incl. GST as of 30 June 2026 (management rounded to INR9,125 crore in closing remarks); average tenure 46 months; over 5x FY26 consolidated revenue; about 7 sites operational in Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh (Rushin's question referenced 9-10 sites).

Diesel: pre-Iran-war bulk price INR88-93/litre; bulk rose to INR112 after 28 March, INR130-140 in April, peaked at INR154 in May; eased to about INR98 in early July and INR110-120 around August 1; barrel-linked price about INR80-82 currently, per management.

Diesel escalation recovery from Coal India of INR10.57 crore in Q1 lifts reported margin from 16.8% to 20.02%; management says normalised margin about 23% (range 22-25%). Management said INR105 crore of Q1 revenue was diesel pass-through, leaving net revenue of INR551 crore.
Pass-through is maximum, not 100%, due to timing mismatch; management attributes Q1 margin dip to diesel spike, calling it a one-off rather than cyclical.

Over 80% of revenue from Coal India; 86% of FY26 revenue from mining (60-50-40% in earlier years per management). Contracts are either overburden-only (paid per cubic metre) or overburden plus coal (paid per cubic metre and per tonne).

Competition: management says it bids on multiple parameters and targets ROCE-disciplined bidding; 8-10 coal and overburden tenders are pending results; no win-rate figure disclosed. Coal demand described as growing on power-sector demand.

adds.what: Fleet of 2,033 units as of June 2026 (no new capacity additions quantified; INR167 crore of IPO proceeds earmarked for new equipment, no unit count given)

growth.why: FY27 guidance of 45-50% revenue growth, 35%+ EBITDA and PAT growth is backed by a INR9,124 crore order book (over 5x FY26 revenue, 46-month average tenure) and INR450 crore of new FY27 orders, with a fleet of 2,033 and INR167 crore of IPO-funded new equipment; EBITDA guidance is contingent on diesel normalising.
